done.why: I'd done the dam-and-river arc all the way through: drained the reservoir, blew up the boat, ran the river and went over the falls on purpose. After I came back I found my trunk where the death message said it would be, and then threw it into the chasm. The thief took my painting. Around then I noticed the world kept turning down my odd phrasings, so I stopped at 59 points.

about: The white house and the Great Underground Empire again, with the most new work spent on Flood Control Dam #3 and the Frigid River. There's a tired old dam, a bubble that waits to be told it may begin, a folded boat with its instructions printed upside down, and a river that hurries off downstream to the falls. It's about working an old machine and then riding out what you've let loose. When you die, a tidy caretaker puts your things back around the house.

ending.what: There was no real ending. I died going over the falls at turn 135, as I meant to, and came back in the forest with empty hands. My score was 59 of 350 when I left.

moments.note: 'kick the mailbox gently' came back as 'You can't see any such thing.' The mailbox was right there. The extra word broke it.
Same thing with 'read leaflet aloud to the house'. Anything added after a noun turns into 'can't see'.
'go in through the window backwards' gave 'can't see any such thing'. What it says is wrong. The problem was my wording, not anything missing.
'climb the unclimbable ramp' was 'not a sentence I recognize', but plain 'west' tried the climb and slid me back down.
The troll ate the lunch. Then it ate the garlic too, with the exact same gracious line.
The dam's description: 'asked to do this for a very long time and has not been thanked.' I liked it.
The bubble has 'the patient look of something waiting to be told it may begin.'
I gave the guidebook to the thief. He thanked me politely, then dumped it as worthless and left disgusted.
Turning the boat pile over and reading the back worked: 'DO NOT INFLATE BY MOUTH, BELLOWS OR VOLCANIC VENT.' Being contrary paid off here.
'take all' at the Reservoir listed everything I was already carrying as 'You already have that!' and didn't even try the trunk.
'take boat' while sitting in it: 'The magic boat cannot go inside itself.'
'listen to the rumbling' gave 'The rumbling makes no sound.' That's odd, since the river had just described it.
I went over the falls on purpose. The new death text says plain things are strewn about the fields, valuables have rolled into a dark corner, and 'somebody tidy has put the lamp back.'
The trunk really was in a dark corner under the house, at East of Chasm, just as the death message said.
It let me throw the trunk into the chasm without a word of protest.
The thief walked through and took the painting before I got it to the case.

wished: I wanted adverbs and trailing phrases ('gently', 'aloud', 'backwards') to be accepted or at least shrugged off, not turned into 'You can't see any such thing.'
I wanted to paddle against the current or steer the boat toward the buoy with my own words.
I wanted to search a room for my lost things after dying.
I wanted to combine items more freely, e.g. squeeze the gunk onto something or pour water into the sack (the bottle had to be opened first).
I wanted to pry the boards off the front door or pull the nails out of the gothic door.
I wanted 'whisper' to do something in the Loud Room.

lines.line: holding back the reservoir to the west with the air of something that has been asked to do this for a very long time and has not been thanked.
lines.why: It made the dam feel like a character and not just a puzzle.

lines.line: It is dark, and has the patient look of something waiting to be told it may begin.
lines.why: It told me the bubble was waiting on something else without telling me what.

lines.line: going downstream as if it had heard something about the end of it and wanted to see for itself.
lines.why: It hinted at the falls, which made me want to go over them.

lines.line: DO NOT INFLATE BY MOUTH, BELLOWS OR VOLCANIC VENT.
lines.why: This was my reward for doing the odd thing and turning the pile over.

lines.line: The magic boat cannot go inside itself.
lines.why: A tidy answer to a silly thing I tried.

lines.line: anything of value has rolled into some dark corner in or under it, and somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
lines.why: The death message tells you where your things went, and it turned out to be true.

lines.line: The engravings translate to "This space intentionally left blank."
lines.why: It's a nice joke when you push on a door that won't open.

fun.why: Most of the fun came from the dam-to-falls run and the jokes I got by being contrary: the boat inside itself, the back of the boat pile, feeding garlic to the troll. Losing the painting and the parser refusing my odd sentences took some of it away.

engagement.why: The dam arc pulled me along: panel, buttons, bolt, reservoir, pump, boat, river. I wanted to see what the falls would do. After I came back to life, finding my trunk kept me going for a while.

difficulty.why: The dam was easy if you read things: the bubble lit after the yellow button, and the wrench turned the bolt. The hardest part was wording. Plain commands worked, but my odd phrasings mostly failed.

interestingness.why: New things on top of the familiar: the turn-the-pile-over instructions, the death message that tells you where your things went, and the dam and river written as if they had moods.

prose.why: The new descriptions are noticeably better and drier than the bare original lines next to them: the dam, the bubble, the river, the chasm. A few replies broke the voice, like 'The rumbling makes no sound' and the blunt 'can't see any such thing' for words it simply didn't understand.
